tools.name: create_grid
tools.description:
POST /: create a grid, your own space of nodes and scores; no API key needed. Returns its `api_key`, shown
only now: pass it as `api_key` to every other tool, or send it as the header `Authorization: Bearer hg-…`.
It holds up to `max_nodes` nodes. Each address may create only a few grids a day.

tools.name: get_grid
tools.description: GET /: the grid the API key opens: its name, and the most nodes it holds, `max_nodes` (null: no limit).

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description:
GET /nodes: the grid's nodes, each with its id, key and emb, in id order. `limit` is 1 to 1024; for the
next page, pass the last id as `cursor`.

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: GET /nodes/{nid}: a node, with its key (null if it has none) and its embedding `emb`.

tools.name: create_node
tools.description:
POST /nodes: add a node. An item gets a `key`, a path unique in the grid (e.g. "/items/42"), so searches
can find it; a query gets none. `emb` is its embedding, 1 to 2048 floats from any model; use one model per
grid. Returns its id and key (not its emb, to keep replies short; get_node has it).

tools.name: update_node
tools.description:
PATCH /nodes/{nid}: change a node. `key`: a new path, or null to remove it, so the node can no longer be
found; leave it out to keep it. `emb`: a new embedding; leave it out to keep it. Its scores keep training,
on the new embedding. Returns its id and key.

tools.name: delete_node
tools.description: DELETE /nodes/{nid}: delete a node and every edge from or to it; its scores no longer train.

tools.name: list_edges
tools.description:
GET /nodes/{nid}/edges: a query's results so far, each an edge with the found node's `id` and its
`score` (null if not scored), in id order. `limit` is 1 to 1024; for the next page, pass the last id as
`cursor`.

tools.name: get_edge
tools.description: GET /nodes/{nid}/edges/{eid}: one result of query `nid`, and its score (null if not scored).

tools.name: create_edge
tools.description:
POST /nodes/{nid}/edges, the search: from query node `nid`, the best node it has not been shown yet,
among those whose key starts with `prefix` ("" for any), stored as a new edge: `id` is the found node's id,
`score` is null until you score it (update_edge). Null when nothing is left. Call again for

tools.name: put_edge
tools.description:
PUT /nodes/{nid}/edges/{eid}: score how well node `eid` fits query `nid`, from -1 (wrong) to 1
(perfect), creating the edge if DNA never suggested it, e.g. scores you already have. Only scores train
DNA; a new score replaces the last.

tools.name: update_edge
tools.description:
PATCH /nodes/{nid}/edges/{eid}: score a result of query `nid` that create_edge returned, from -1 (wrong)
to 1 (perfect). Only scores train DNA; a new score replaces the last.

tools.name: delete_edge
tools.description:
DELETE /nodes/{nid}/edges/{eid}: forget a result, so it can be suggested again; its score no longer
trains.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_grid" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_edge · Private data: create_grid, get_grid · Public sink: create_grid, create_node, create_edge · Destructive: update_node, delete_node, delete_edge.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_edge · Private data: create_grid, get_grid · Public sink: create_grid, create_node, create_edge · Destructive: update_node, delete_node, delete_edge

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
